$comment: Cache policy for the 2140.wtf zone, applied as the entrypoint of the
http_request_cache_settings phase. Rules are evaluated in order and the
first match wins, so the order below IS the policy: hashed assets, then
unhashed media, then everything that must never be cached at the edge.
Why HTML is never cached here: GitHub Pages serves this app as a static
SPA, and every build renames the bundles (/assets/index-<hash>.js). An
edge-cached index.html or route shell would keep pointing browsers at
assets the new deploy already removed, which fails as a blank page, not
as a stale-looking page. HTML therefore always goes to the origin.
Requests that match no rule fall back to the zone's default behaviour
(cache_level standard: static extensions only, respecting origin TTL).
name: 2140.wtf cache policy
description: Immutable hashed assets at the edge; HTML, route shells, the service worker and the web manifest always from the origin.

rules.description: Hashed build output (/assets/index-<hash>.js|css, fonts, images): immutable, one year.
Unhashed static media and fonts (public/ files keep their names across builds): short edge TTL, quick browser revalidation.
Documents and app entry points: .html, the extensionless route shells (/chat, /bao/markets, ...), the service worker and the web manifest. Never cached at the edge.
rules.expression: (ends_with(http.request.uri.path, ".html") or ends_with(http.request.uri.path, "/sw.js") or ends_with(http.request.uri.path, ".webmanifest") or not(matches(http.request.uri.path, "\.[a-z0-9]+$")))
